answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol assigns work through a capped, randomized queue, then slashes stake when independently verifiable results fail a challenge. Splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply its influence: each identity must tie up capital, and cheating risks losing it. Like a jetty protecting an orchard, the stake is a costly boundary, not proof of unique personhood; saffron-colored labels add nothing.
